## Tyrannosaurus rex Skull

   * Tyrannosaurus rex*
Hell Creek Formation, Montana, USA (~66–68 million years old)

This 3D model is based on the famous MOR 555 “Wankel Rex” specimen, one of the most scientifically important Tyrannosaurus rex fossils ever discovered. The specimen was found in Montana, USA, in 1988 and excavated between 1989–1990 from the Hell Creek Formation.

The skull preserves the deep, powerfully reinforced anatomy characteristic of mature tyrannosaurs. Fused nasal bones, thick serrated teeth, and massive jaw musculature allowed T. rex to generate one of the strongest bite forces among terrestrial animals. Large eye sockets and expanded olfactory regions indicate advanced vision and an exceptional sense of smell.

This specimen is also famous for contributing to groundbreaking studies on microscopic soft-tissue preservation in dinosaur fossils. _(Based on digital data from the Smithsonian Institution 3D Digitization Program. Original scan and digital asset by the Smithsonian Institution.)

name: Camponotus gigas
description:
D. gigas is a large species of ant, native to Southeast Asian forests. It is one of the largest ants in existence, measuring in at 20.9 mm for normal workers, and 28.1 mm for the soldiers. 礁池の砂まじりの岩礁に棲んでいる。マガキガイに似ているが、殻表はなめらかで、体層の縫合がねじれている。殻口は狭く、内面は紫紅色で、多数の螺状糸がある。奄美諸島以南、熱帯西太平洋。

name: オウムガイ / Nautilus
description:
生きた化石として有名なオウムガイは、4億年以上もその姿を変えていない。貝の仲間ではなく、イカ・タコなどの頭足綱に属する。貝殻の内部は多くの隔室に仕切られ、100本もの吸盤のない短い腕をもった軟体部が入っている。よく間違えられるが、オウムガイの先祖はアンモナイトではない。アンモナイトはオウムガイから分化した仲間。

Famous as a “living fossil,” the nautilus has remained virtually unchanged for over 400 million years. It is not a mollusk but belongs to the class Cephalopoda, which includes squids and octopuses. The interior of its shell is divided into many chambers, housing a soft body with short arms bearing as many as 100 suckerless tentacles. Although often mistaken, the nautilus is not descended from the ammonite; rather, the ammonite is a group that diverged from the nautilus.
